title.value: Gated Orthogonal Recurrent Units: On Learning to Forget
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the primary focus of the paper which is on Gated Orthogonal Recurrent Units and their ability to learn to forget, as mentioned in the introduction and the abstract.
title.quote: We present a novel recurrent neural network (RNN) based model that combines the remembering ability of unitary RNNs with the ability of gated RNNs to effectively forget redundant/irrelevant information in its memory.

analysis.description: This paper introduces a novel recurrent neural network architecture called the Gated Orthogonal Recurrent Unit (GORU), which combines the advantages of unitary and orthogonal recurrent networks with a forgetting mechanism typical of gated recurrent units.

type.justification: The paper provides empirical results through experiments on several benchmark tasks to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed GORU model compared to other models.
type.quote: We empirically both show the orthogonal/unitary RNNs lack the ability to forget and also the ability of GORU to simultaneously remember long term dependencies while forgetting irrelevant information.

name.justification: The paper primarily focuses on recurrent neural networks, specifically advancing the architecture with the introduction of GORU.
name.quote: We present a novel recurrent neural network (RNN) based model that combines the remembering ability of unitary RNNs with the ability of gated RNNs to effectively forget redundant/irrelevant information in its memory.

name.justification: The inclusion of tasks like bAbI Question Answering points towards applications in NLP.
name.quote: Our model is able to outperform LSTMs, GRUs and Unitary RNNs on several long-term dependency benchmark tasks. We provide competitive results along with an analysis of our model on many natural sequential tasks including the bAbI Question Answering.

name.justification: The paper evaluates the model on tasks like TIMIT speech spectrum prediction which is a common task in speech recognition.
name.quote: We provide competitive results along with an analysis of our model on many natural sequential tasks including... TIMIT speech spectrum prediction.

name.justification: The paper discusses synthetic tasks such as algorithmic tasks to evaluate the model's ability to handle long-term dependencies and noisy inputs.
name.quote: GORU outperforms a recent variation of unitary RNN called EURNN (Jing et al. 2016) on language modeling, denoising, parenthesis and the question answering tasks... algorithmic, parenthesis and the denoising tasks.

name.justification: The GORU model is the main contribution of the paper, combining the strengths of unitary and gated RNNs.
name.quote: We propose a new architecture, the Gated Orthogonal Recurrent Unit (GORU), which combines the advantages of the above two frameworks, namely (i) the ability to capture long term dependencies by using orthogonal matrices and (ii) the ability to “forget” by using a GRU structure.

is_contributed.justification: The GORU is introduced as a novel model in the paper.
is_contributed.quote: We propose a new architecture, the Gated Orthogonal Recurrent Unit (GORU)

is_executed.justification: The paper conducts experiments using the GORU model, implying its execution.
is_executed.quote: We demonstrate that GORU is able to learn long term dependencies effectively, even in complicated datasets which require a forgetting ability.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares GORU with other models like LSTM, GRU, and EURNN across various tasks.
is_compared.quote: On question answering, speech spectrum prediction, algorithmic, parenthesis and the denoising tasks, GORU achieves better accuracy on the test set over all other models that we compare against.

referenced_paper_title.justification: GORU is a new contribution by this paper, so no prior reference exists for it.
referenced_paper_title.quote: We propose a new architecture, the Gated Orthogonal Recurrent Unit (GORU)

name.justification: The bAbI dataset is used in the paper to test the episodic question answering capabilities of their model.
name.quote: We tested the ability of our RNN models on a word-level episodic question answering task. The bAbI dataset (Weston et al. ) examines RNN’s ability to understand language and perform basic logical reasoning.

name.quote: We test each RNN on character-level language modeling. The RNN is fed by one character each step from a real context and supposed to output the prediction for the next character. We used the Penn Treebank corpus.
